% Pictures turned over or lowered below the baseline, wider than a phone's
% column: TikZ pictures turned over, also flattened, and lowered by a
% baseline, with and without being turned over; \includegraphics turned
% over at the text width, wider than the text, and at a natural size wider
% than the text; and a narrow picture turned over. A picture turned over
% hangs below the baseline in the PDF, as graphics.sty swaps its height
% and depth. On any screen, the share of each picture below the baseline
% is the share in the PDF, also where the picture is shrunk to the column.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage{tikz}
\begin{document}
Drawn: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\tikz\fill (0,0) rectangle (0.9\textwidth,2cm);} after.

Flattened: \scalebox{1}[-0.5]{\tikz\fill (0,0) rectangle (0.9\textwidth,2cm);} after.

Lowered: \tikz[baseline=0.5cm]\fill (0,0) rectangle (0.9\textwidth,2cm); after.

Lowered and turned over: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\tikz[baseline=0.5cm]\fill (0,0) rectangle (0.9\textwidth,2cm);} after.

Narrow: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\tikz\fill (0,0) rectangle (2cm,1cm);} after.

Text width: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\includegraphics[alt={text width}, width=\textwidth]{test-picture.png}} after.

Wider: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\includegraphics[alt={wider}, width=1.2\textwidth]{test-picture.png}} after.

Natural: \scalebox{1}[-1]{\includegraphics[alt={natural}]{test-wide.png}} after.
\end{document}
